candidates.lead: Sir Billy Boston was "a pioneer" and "an inspiration" and his legacy will continue, Wigan Council says
candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Council renames town square in honour of Sir Billy Boston - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Sir Billy Boston already has a statue and a plaque in the square now named after him By Paul Burnell North West , Reporting from in Wigan Published 1 hour ago Rugby League star Sir Billy Boston is to be further honoured in his adopted hometown Wigan, with the renaming of the town's square where his statue is situated. Sir Billy, who was Rugby league's first knight, died last month, aged 92. His funeral took place at Wigan Warriors' Brick Community Stadium on Thursday. Believe Square will now be called Sir Billy Boston Square "to ensure his legacy continues" in the heart of the town, Wigan Council has announced. In March, a civic service was held to mark a new plaque being added to his statue, following his knighthood in 2025. 'An inspiration' Born in Cardiff in 1934, Sir Billy grew up playing rugby union but faced prejudice because of his ethnicity and was overlooked by his home club. He came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old. Wigan Council leader Nazia Rehman said Sir Billy was "more than a sporting legend, he was a pioneer, an inspiration, and someone who brought immense pride to Wigan Borough". Image caption, The statue of Sir Billy Boston in Believe Square, Wigan, was unveiled in 2016 Rehman said: "Following his passing, we wanted to ensure his legacy continues to be honoured in the heart of our town. "That's why we are renaming Believe Square, the home of Sir Billy's statue, as Sir Billy Boston Square." She said it was a "fitting tribute to a remarkable man whose achievements broke barriers, inspired generations, and will never be forgotten". "Sir Billy's legacy will live on in Wigan, forever," she added. Sir Billy reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches and claimed 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship. He was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side and was the first black British player to tour Australia and New Zealand. Wigan's chief executive Kris Radlinski said: "For generations, people will pass though the [sqaure], children will walk with their families, people who never had the privilege to see Billy play will see his name and ask who he was, and another generation will tell his story." Image source, PA Media Image caption, Sir Billy scored two tries for Wigan in the 1959 rugby league Challenge Cup final at Wembley The player scored 571 tries in his career - a total surpassed only by Australian legend Brian Bevan in top-class rugby league. The bronze statue of Sir Billy in Wigan's Believe Square was unveiled in 2016 . There is also a statue of the rugby league great in his home town of Cardiff as well as one outside Wembley stadium and he has been recognised for helping to open doors for black players in sport. Sir Billy, who had dementia for more than 10 years, was awarded his knighthood before the King's birthday honours list was officially announced last year because of concerns over his health. candidates.lead: Thomas White has been transferred from a secure psychiatric hospital back to prison, his family say
candidates.evidence_text: Family's fears for Thomas White as he is sent back to jail - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Clara White (right), pictured with Thomas White and his mother, said she was calling for the government to establish a clear timeline and plan to resolve the IPP injustice By Angela Ferguson North West Published 10 September 2026 The family of a man serving an indefinite prison sentence say they fear for his health after he was transferred back to jail from a secure psychiatric hospital. Thomas White, 43, was given an Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence for stealing a mobile phone in 2012. The sentences, which have no fixed release date, were abolished four months later. His sister, Clara White, said he was "a severely unwell man who needs treatment, stability and hope". The Ministry of Justice has been approached for comment. Clara said the family "felt a small sense of hope" when White was moved from HMP Manchester to a secure psychiatric hospital, but now say "he is being sent back into the very system that made him ill". She said her brother, who has a teenage son, had already been moved between 14 prisons and that this latest transfer would make it his 15th in 14 years. While he needed treatment and support, he was instead being "sent back to prison with no release date and no certainty about what his future holds", she said. White had been binge-drinking in Manchester before he stole a phone from two Christian missionaries in 2012. He was given an IPP sentence with a minimum tariff of two years. His family said he has now spent more than 14 years in custody, serving more than seven times that period. The family's calls for the government to step in come days after Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to tackle the issue of IPP sentences as part of efforts to address prison overcrowding. Clara said: "Andy Burnham's pledge to resolve the IPP injustice is a welcome first step, but we now need a clear timeline and plan from the government." Image source, White family photograph Image caption, Thomas White's sister has previously said his prolonged imprisonment has "ruined" both of their lives Self-harm attempts White's family said he was transferred from HMP Manchester to a secure psychiatric hospital in Northumberland in November 2025 after years of severe mental deterioration. They said he had developed paranoid schizophrenia while serving his IPP sentence and that an independent psychiatrist concluded that his indefinite imprisonment was the probable cause of his illness. The move followed a six-year campaign by his family and interventions from former Home Secretary Lord Blunkett and former Prisons Minister Lord Timpson. White's family said he had also made attempts to harm himself in prison and feared his return would risk undoing the progress made during treatment. Clara White said IPP prisoners were expected to complete rehabilitation programmes to demonstrate reduced risk and secure release, but the multiple transfers her brother had faced meant he had never been given a realistic opportunity to complete them. In 2016, while held at HMP Norwich, White began speaking in Roman numerals during calls home. He was also reportedly seen walking the prison wing wrapped in a bedsheet, presenting himself as Jesus Christ and telling fellow prisoners he could heal them. What are IPP sentences? IPP sentences were introduced in 2005 and intended for the perpetrators of serious crimes and persistent criminals. They were scrapped in 2012, but the change was not applied retrospectively. More than 2,000 people are still in prison on IPP sentences, according to the United Nations, (UN), who have called for the end of IPP sentences. , external In July, the United Nations described the continuation of IPP sentences as "perpetuating serious human rights violations". The human rights body said nearly all unreleased IPP prisoners have served terms beyond their original tariff periods, while almost three-quarters have spent more than a decade in prison beyond the punishment originally considered necessary by the sentencing court. candidates.lead: The walkways will connect parts of Manchester city centre to other places, including the Etihad campus
candidates.evidence_text: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme - BBC News Image caption, The CyanLines project will see a number of "floating walkways" connecting different parts of Manchester By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 10 September 2026 Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed. It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade. The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." There are two further CyanLines routes in development in Newton Heath and Rusholme. Backing for the plans comes from the Manchester and Trafford councils, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City FC, the Canal and River Trust, property developers Renaker and Urban Splash, and the National Trust, among others. Pete Bradshaw, director of sustainability at Manchester City, said: "The plans for the CyanLines route add a new layer of nature-rich, innovative and imaginative active travel and community experiences for fans, visitors and those living and working in the neighbourhood." Image caption, The next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct park project has also been announced Funding for the next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct "garden in the sky" was also announced. Part of the old railway line has been transformed into a public park, which opened in 2022. The second phase will expand it to the full 330-metre length of the Victorian-era structure. It is being supported by the Bupa Foundation's Healthy Cities programme. Hilary McGrady, director-general at the National Trust, said: "Bupa's funding will help the Trust extend the sky park project in Manchester, meaning more people will experience and benefit from this green space that sits in the heart of the city." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Friends, family and players past and present have gathered to pay their respects at the funeral of Wigan rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston Boston, the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood, died last month aged 92 His funeral took place at Wigan Warriors' Brick Community Stadium, with mourners including many of the club's current squad Before the service, a cortege travelled through Wigan , external on its route towards the stadium in the Greater Manchester town. A private burial ceremony was set to follow At the request of the Boston family, mourners were encouraged to wear traditional funeral attire Items of Wigan Warriors' cherry red and white could also be worn, including scarves, ties and headwear

candidates.summary: Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade The recently announced rout

candidates.lead: Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade The recently announced rout
candidates.evidence_text: Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." There are two further CyanLines routes in development in Newton Heath and Rusholme Backing for the plans comes from the Manchester and Trafford councils, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City FC, the Canal and River Trust, property developers Renaker and Urban Splash, and the National Trust, among others

candidates.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 Arsonists were caught on CCTV breaking into a business and starting a fire while one of them was still inside. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. candidates.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Goodbye, Sir Billy Boston Wigan said goodbye to a local hero Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 16:09, 10 Sep 2026 Updated 17:07, 10 Sep 2026 View 7 Images Sir Billy Boston funeral procession outside Wigan Town Hall (Image: Sean Hansfor The sight of a jet black hearse drew rapturous applause all across the streets of Wigan today as the town bid farewell to one of its greatest adopted sons Sir Billy Boston was laid to rest following a poignant funeral service at the Brick Community Stadium on Thursday (September 10) Following the announcement of Billy's death, tributes poured in from the Prime Ministers to rugby league bosses. However, today was the time for the people of Wigan to commemorate the mild mannered gent who became one of their own Before the service, a funeral cortege passed through Wigan. Snaking its way through the town from the Bold Hotel to the sports stadium One of the streets that the procession passed through were Swan Meadow Road and Pool Street, where hundreds of Wiganers congregated outside the Honey Suckle Inn to pay their respects

candidates.summary: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou

candidates.lead: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou
candidates.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 Arsonists were caught on CCTV breaking into a business and starting a fire while one of them was still inside. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. The third man, who was behind the shutters, was seen on CCTV fleeing like a 'scalded cat', appearing to be on fire After the flames died down, he joined the other two in the car before it sped off. Firefigthers raced to the scene and the blaze was extinguished. Around £300,000 of damage was caused at the bedding supply business

candidates.evidence_text: Burnage Labour wins Burnage by-election in crucial seat as 'Burnham bounce' credited with making a difference Labour has held its seat in Burnage Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 01:31, 11 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Labour's Carl Austin Labour have won the Burnage by-election to hold onto former council leader Bev Craig’s old seat Councillor Carl Austin-Behan was elected on Thursday night (September 10) picking up 1,365 votes in a race which was expected to be ‘very close’ with the Greens. In the end Green Party candidate Daoud Nawaz got a total of 1,037 ballots The vote on September 10 was triggered back in July when Bev Craig was elected as Greater Manchester mayor, requiring her to stand down as a councillor in the Burnage ward and as leader of Manchester City Council New Burnage Councillor Carl Austin-Behan said he felt ‘honoured’ that residents had put their trust in him once again after previously being elected to the ward from 2011 to 2018 View 3 Images Daoud Nawaz came second for the Green Party (Image: Jason Roberts / Manchester Evening News)

candidates.evidence_text: Politics LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 6 hours ago Burnage by-election RECAP as Labour HOLD mayor Bev Craig's former council seat in fight against Greens Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour in a close and crucial by-election A smiling Carl Austi Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour, beating his main rival, Green Party's Daoud Nawaz The race was tipped as a ‘huge’ moment for the city’s future with the Greens gunning to make a ‘statement’ by taking the former council leader’s seat, which has boundaries covering Burnage and parts of southern Levenshulme The seat with nearly 14,000 voters was up for grabs after former Manchester City Council leader Ms Craig was elected as mayor of Greater Manchester in July While the outcome in Burnage tonight won’t have a drastic impact on the overall control of the council which is comfortably in Labour’s hands, it could be a sign of things to come with the May 2027 local elections now just eight months away Manchester council is run by the Labour Party, which holds 63 seats in the city, next to the opposition Greens with 21, seven Reform UK councillors, and four Lib Dems

candidates.lead: Alderley Edge Three cars seized after 'illegal' Alderley Edge 'car meet' A force said large-scale car meets were a 'real issue' for locals Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 21:04, 10 Sep 2026 View 2 Images A blue BMW M4 which was one of the t Police have seized three car
candidates.evidence_text: Alderley Edge Three cars seized after 'illegal' Alderley Edge 'car meet' A force said large-scale car meets were a 'real issue' for locals Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 21:04, 10 Sep 2026 View 2 Images A blue BMW M4 which was one of the t Police have seized three cars following a 'car meet' in Alderley Edge Cheshire Police said there were 'illegal car meetings' which took place in and around the leafy village on Sunday, August 30, which led to complaints about 'dangerous and anti-social driving.' Officers carried out enquiries afterwards and the force said they identified three cars they said had, amongst others, 'committed traffic offences.' "These offences included vehicles being driven without due care and attention and drivers being seen to use a phone whilst behind the wheel" they said in a statement issued today (Thursday, September 10) As a result three cars, a blue BMW M4, a white Toyota Supra and a black BMW M140i, were tracked down and seized under section 59 of the Road Traffic Act

candidates.summary: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close

candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed.
candidates.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council

The site, known as The Elms, was previously home to a Victorian Bury council had planned to dispose of the site to a developer, but has now said it intends to carry out the project itself. This means it will have greater control over the final scheme and the new homes would be added to the council’s housing stock, generating new income for th The authority’s cabinet signed off on the move at a meeting last night. Lead member for regeneration and growth Charlotte Morris said the scheme is ‘in line’ with the council’s ‘ambitions and vision’ to deliver affordable homes and build on brownfield sites ‘first’ However, that pronouncement was met with scorn from some in the public gallery. One woman, whose name was just given as Amanda, interrupted the meeting to dispute the council’s ‘brownfield first’ claim

The funeral service is being held at The Brick Community Stadium - the home of Wigan Warriors - at 12.30 pm on Thursday. Entry to the stadium is controlled by pre-allocated Before the service, a funeral cortege passed through Wigan this morning, starting at 11.20am at the Bold Hotel. Wigan Warriors' first team will also be in attendance to give Sir Billy a guard of honour as he makes his final journey." Last year, Sir Billy made more history when he became the first rugby league player to be knighted after he was honoured by King Charles at Buckingham Palace

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Rural Bolton quarry due to close this year asks to extend operations until 2031 Harwood Quarry is only one of two in the country that can produce the shale needed to create high-quality bricks Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 14 A long-standing rural quarry is seeking to expend its operations for another five years Harwood Quarry, on the north east outskirts of Bolton , has seen shale extracted from the ground to make bricks for generations, but its licence is due to expire at the end of 2026 A planning application has been lodged to extend that period until 2031, due to what the company said was ‘cumulative commercial and practical factors, beyond its control’ Booth Ventures Ltd, which runs the site, said those reasons included disruption caused by the Covid pandemic, significant increases in energy and construction costs and difficulties within the regional and national construction sector The firm said that has affected its delivery programme and delayed its completion by the deadline of December 31, 2026

Between now and 2029, the local authority will receive £6m The decision reallocate £1m to continue the scheme will provide eligible families with continued financial support during the remaining school holiday periods of the 2026/27 financial year, giving additional support at a time when the cost of feeding children can place extra pres Before the government expanded free school meals, there were nearly 16,000 children eligible across the borough in 2024. A 2026 cabinet report said there were 17,410 live claims and over a quarter of children in Salford were ;living in absolute low income families in 2023/24′ The move was broadly welcomed by cabinet members who praised the support provided against a backdrop of families struggling with the cost of living. Criticisms were also levelled over the current income threshold for free school meals for being too low

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS He was told it was 'just a virus', now he blinks to communicate The aspiring DJ and fitness fanatic has been left paralysed following the doctor's blunder News Tom Bevan and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 08:01, 11 Sep 2026 View 6 Images Oli Copp A fitness fanatic has been left paralysed after a brain condition was dismissed by an A&E doctor as a virus. Oli Coppock, from Warrington , turned up to hospital with an overnight bag when he first felt unwell But the 34-year-old was sent home from Warrington Hospital and told to take paracetamol. The aspiring DJ and Manchester United fan went on to suffer a cardiac arrest Fluid on his brain was discovered at a later CT scan, and Oli was diagnosed with inoperable brain stem damage. Oli is now non-verbal - and his family have sued the NHS over the blunder Dad Stephen Coppock said: "Warrington [Hospital] should hold their heads in shame. As far as I am concerned, the health service that he trusted to protect him has destroyed my boy by failing to do the basics and his life was ruined at 32 now he is a shell of his former self "They robbed him of his life. Every day is like a lifetime for him as his mind is still completely active and he knows exactly what is going on but his body can't respond

candidates.evidence_text: National news Mother of boy, 7, killed in BMW crash speaks of enduring grief 'I can’t accept that Jack has gone and I never will' Comments News Andrew Robinson and Paul Britton Reporter 08:00, 11 Sep 2026 Updated 08:01, 11 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Jack A mother told of her enduring grief as a motorist was jailed for causing the death of her seven year-old son by driving without insurance In an emotional court statement, Jack Rooke's mum said she 'can't accept that Jack has gone and I never will'. The boy died after being hit by a BMW X4 being driven by Nathan Shaw in Huddersfield Shaw, of Tudor Street, Huddersfield, was sentenced at Leeds Crown Court on Thursday for driving offences following Jack's death in Golcar on August 30, 2023 The 35-year-old was sentenced to 42 months in prison after pleading guilty to causing death while driving without insurance and two perverting the course of justice offences. He was also disqualified from driving for 57 months In a victim personal statement, Jack’s mother said each day was a struggle without her beautiful and loving boy and that her life had been wrecked by his death. She also described the massive impact Jack’s loss had on his sisters , including Mya who had lost her best friend

candidates.evidence_text: Trains Faster trains, battery power, more jobs, as Andy Burnham announces £1bn plan for the north "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came" News Sophie Wingate, PA and Stephen Topping Se Andy Burnham has announced a £1 billion investment which should bring faster and 'more reliable' trains to Manchester and the north A new TransPennine Express fleet of 29 battery-electric trains will cut journey times by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds, and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York, the government says The new trains will run on routes between Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull. They should be built from 2028 and enter service from the end of 2034 The Prime Minister said: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came. And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities "Today that starts to change. These 29 new trains will bring faster, more reliable journeys to the North, and thousands of British jobs for the next generation. It's exactly what Great British Railways is all about - taking back control of the basics and getting Britain believing

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan The site 'pivotal in shaping Wigan's future' Westwood Park has been described as 'a new gateway to Wigan town centre' News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Westwood Park (Image: Wigan council) A plan for one of Wigan’s largest development sites is out for public consultation over the next six weeks. candidates.summary: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou

candidates.lead: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Cou
candidates.evidence_text: Cheetham Hill 'Let's do this mission today': Snapchatting arsonists thought they had the perfect plan - now they've been locked up Diogo Cabral and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes have been jailed following the 'nasty' attack View Image Diogo Cabral, left, a Comments News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:03, 11 Sep 2026 Arsonists were caught on CCTV breaking into a business and starting a fire while one of them was still inside. Portuguese nationals Diogo Cabral, 21, and Emanuel Feliciano Simoes, 36, organised the attack on Snapchat, car "Let's do this mission today," one message discovered by detectives read. Manchester Crown Court heard they were seen pulling up in a car outside Shzsr Enterprises Ltd, on Broughton Street, Cheetham Hill at around midnight on March 1, 2023 They prised open the shutters with crowbars before two of them ran back to the car and grabbing bottles of accelerant. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. The third man, who was behind the shutters, was seen on CCTV fleeing like a 'scalded cat', appearing to be on fire After the flames died down, he joined the other two in the car before it sped off. Firefigthers raced to the scene and the blaze was extinguished. Around £300,000 of damage was caused at the bedding supply business

candidates.evidence_text: Politics LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 6 hours ago Burnage by-election RECAP as Labour HOLD mayor Bev Craig's former council seat in fight against Greens Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour in a close and crucial by-election A smiling Carl Austi Carl Austin-Behan has held the seat for Labour, beating his main rival, Green Party's Daoud Nawaz The race was tipped as a ‘huge’ moment for the city’s future with the Greens gunning to make a ‘statement’ by taking the former council leader’s seat, which has boundaries covering Burnage and parts of southern Levenshulme The seat with nearly 14,000 voters was up for grabs after former Manchester City Council leader Ms Craig was elected as mayor of Greater Manchester in July While the outcome in Burnage tonight won’t have a drastic impact on the overall control of the council which is comfortably in Labour’s hands, it could be a sign of things to come with the May 2027 local elections now just eight months away Manchester council is run by the Labour Party, which holds 63 seats in the city, next to the opposition Greens with 21, seven Reform UK councillors, and four Lib Dems

Officers carried out enquiries afterwards and the force said they identified three cars they said had, amongst others, 'committed traffic offences.' candidates.summary: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close

candidates.lead: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed.
candidates.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council

candidates.lead: Whitefield 'You say brownfield sites come first.
candidates.evidence_text: Whitefield 'You say brownfield sites come first. Absolutely not. There’s hectares and hectares of greenbelt you’re destroying' Plans for over-55s flats in Whitefield are met with scorn from public gallery Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:01, 10 Sep Bury council has revealed ambitions to build new homes on vacant land in Whitefield - but one member of the public gave a scornful objection to the council's 'brownfield first' boast The scheme, off Elms Close, is expected to create 16 affordable flats for residents over the age of 55, with the council saying this would promote independent living and help meet the needs of an ‘ageing population’. The site, known as The Elms, was previously home to a Victorian Bury council had planned to dispose of the site to a developer, but has now said it intends to carry out the project itself. This means it will have greater control over the final scheme and the new homes would be added to the council’s housing stock, generating new income for th The authority’s cabinet signed off on the move at a meeting last night. Lead member for regeneration and growth Charlotte Morris said the scheme is ‘in line’ with the council’s ‘ambitions and vision’ to deliver affordable homes and build on brownfield sites ‘first’ However, that pronouncement was met with scorn from some in the public gallery. One woman, whose name was just given as Amanda, interrupted the meeting to dispute the council’s ‘brownfield first’ claim

Simon Richardson, 35, pleaded not guilty to murdering Mr Mullins. He died following an incident on April 20 this year Mr Richardson, of no fixed address, but formerly of Epsom Avenue in Sale, also pleaded not guilty to manslaughter and dangerous driving, by driving a Ford Transit van on roads including Williams Street, Oldham Road, Wellington Street, Peace Street, Wickentree Lane, Wrigley Head a He is due to go on trial next month at Minshull Street Crown Court. Emergency services were called to reports of a collision involving a car and a cyclist on Paddock Lane, in Dunham Massey near Altrincham, at around 6.10pm on April 20 The cyclist, Mr Mullins, 56, died at the scene. He had been headteacher of Stretford Grammar School for 17 years Judge Maurice Greene told Mr Richardson, who appeared in court by video link: “Your trial will be on October 13. There will be a pre-trial review, as things stand, on October 2. You will remain in custody.”

candidates.evidence_text: Paul Dennett Salford postcode lottery fears as parents issued with £1m update ahead of school holidays Thousands of children could benefit from the decision made today but concerns remain about the impact of recent government changes Comments News Edw Salford council will look to lobby the government over fears an expansion of free school meals could become a ‘postcode lottery’ without more support. It comes as more than 16,000 children could benefit from support over the holidays At the council’s Cabinet meeting today (8 September), it was agreed to continue the city’s existing school holiday food support scheme for the October half-term, Christmas holidays and February half-term. Between now and 2029, the local authority will receive £6m The decision reallocate £1m to continue the scheme will provide eligible families with continued financial support during the remaining school holiday periods of the 2026/27 financial year, giving additional support at a time when the cost of feeding children can place extra pres Before the government expanded free school meals, there were nearly 16,000 children eligible across the borough in 2024. A 2026 cabinet report said there were 17,410 live claims and over a quarter of children in Salford were ;living in absolute low income families in 2023/24′ The move was broadly welcomed by cabinet members who praised the support provided against a backdrop of families struggling with the cost of living. Criticisms were also levelled over the current income threshold for free school meals for being too low

Emma Murray, 33, flew into a rage and threw the glass against a wall after accusing Allen Smith of being unreceptive when she was telling him something. But the tumbler shattered on impact - sending a shard of glass into Mr Smith's face and causing a laceration to his eye Police called by Murray herself subsequently arrived at the scene and arrested her. When quizzed she said: ''I didn't mean for this to happen. I threw the glass out of frustration. Allen often does not listen to what I have to say.'' At Warrington Magistrates' Court Murray, of Laurel Walk in Partington , pleaded guilty to assault by beating and was fined £120 and ordered that she pay £133 in costs and surcharge. candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Credit: planning documents Conlon cracks on with Wigan SEND work 10 September 2026 11:43 Neil Tague Comments (0) The Preston contractor is to deliver an £18m project that will provide a new home for Hope School & College. The relocation of the school from Kelvin Grove to Central Park off Montrose Avenue was consulted on as far back as 2019, and was approved in 2024. Wigan Council was the applicant, with Michael Hyde & Associates the architect. Documents filed in August with the local authority show Conlon stepping up the delivery programme, with the submission of a construction and environmental management plan. As set out in this document, the main works consist of building two new single-storey classroom blocks, predominantly of steel frame construction, along with the refurbishment of an existing 1980s two-storey block, to be used as the main administration building. Conlon said that all accessible windows and doors have been hoarded with steel shuttering for security. Proposed works include full interior strip-out, new windows/doors, removal of existing partitions ad their replacement with new partitions. Associated external works include car parking, pupil playgrounds and courtyard, and landscaping. Conlon is busy in education: the employee-owned firm is also on board as contractor for the Crewe primary school approved this week by Cheshire East. The business has already delivered a number of SEN and SEND projects as main contractor, including Springwood School in Salford, which opened in time for this month’s intake of pupils, Highfurlong School in Blackpool in 2025, and Springfield School in Wilmslow in 2024. candidates.lead: The group is planning to open new offices in Manchester city centre and Cheshire
candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham law firm celebrates 25 years with record £10m fee income Skip to content News — Business Altrincham law firm celebrates 25 years with record £10m fee income The group is planning to open new offices in Manchester city centre and Cheshire. , and David Prior September 10, 2026 . 12:27 PM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email An Altrincham-headquartered law firm has celebrated its 25th anniversary by recording fee income of more than £10 million for the first time. McHale Group, which employs 152 people across five offices, passed the milestone in the year to May 31 and has now outlined plans for further expansion. The group is planning to open new offices in Manchester city centre and Cheshire over the next 12 months, while discussions over the acquisition of two other firms are said to be at an advanced stage. It is also expanding its Altrincham headquarters at Warrant House, where it has taken an additional 4,500 sq ft to accommodate the growth of its real estate team. Plans are already under way to take further space in the building. McHale & Co was founded by Andrew McHale in Levenshulme in 2001, initially specialising in criminal law before expanding into conveyancing. Over the subsequent 25 years, it has grown both organically and through acquisitions into a full-service legal group, with offices in Altrincham, Stockport, Heywood, London and Solihull. Andrew moved into the role of group chairman earlier this year, with Adam Horner and Kamil Tomaszewski taking over as joint chief executives. “It’s been a rollercoaster ride over the past 25 years, and I feel blessed that so many great people have been part of the journey,” said Andrew. Founder Andrew McHale (centre) with joint chief executives Kamil Tomaszewski (left) and Adam Horner “I’m so grateful to our team, clients, partners and referrers who have been so pivotal in our evolution over the years. “In some ways, it feels as though we are just getting started. I’m hugely excited about what Adam and Kamil can achieve as they lead the group into its next chapter.” The record year has also seen a series of senior appointments and a six-figure investment in staff training, including an expansion of the group's in-house leadership academy. Around 45 employees are currently taking part in monthly development sessions. The group now provides legal services spanning areas including family law, residential property, employment, personal injury and medical negligence, as well as corporate, commercial litigation, real estate and intellectual property work. It also has a specialist sports practice advising professional sportspeople and teams on contracts, transfers and commercial opportunities, and is looking to add immigration advice to its business services. Joint chief executive Adam Horner said reaching the 25th anniversary alongside a record financial year was “a huge achievement”. “As we look ahead, we have a clear and ambitious strategy for the next phase of our growth,” he said. “We will continue to invest in our people, strengthen our specialist teams and expand our presence across the North West, with new offices and carefully targeted acquisitions forming an important part of our plans.” McHale Group marked its anniversary with a celebration at Bowdon Cricket Club attended by almost 400 staff, family members, friends of the firm and other guests. candidates.evidence_text: Fly-tipping offences could face tougher penalties under new plans from Manchester City Council, which is proposing to increase Fixed Penalty Notices (FPNs) for serious cases to the maximum amount Offenders caught committing fly-tipping offences will now face a £1,000 fine, an increase from the current £700 penalty. Those who pay within 10 days will be eligible for a reduced payment of £700, with the full amount payable within 14 days. The landmark decision is subject to a The move is part of a wider commitment to tackle environmental crime and support the ambitions set out in Manchester's new Fly-tipping and Litter Strategy, which aims to reduce fly-tipping incidents by a third by 2035 Residents have repeatedly said cleaner streets, well-kept parks and action on environmental crime as among their top priorities for the city. Fly-tipping continues to place a significant burden on council resources, drain public money away from essential services and impact the h In 2025-26, Manchester recorded 17,954 fly-tipping incidents, resulting in the removal of more than 5,594 tonnes of waste from across the city. A total of 992 fines were issued for waste deposits in the same period The strategy supports the aims of the council's Our Manchester Strategy , which sets out a vision for cleaner, greener and better maintained neighbourhoods

candidates.evidence_text: Cllr Garry Bridges is set to be appointed as the new Leader of Manchester City Council at a special meeting this week (Thursday 3 September, 6pm) Cllr Bridges succeeds Cllr Bev Craig, who was elected as Greater Manchester Mayor in July, having previously served as statutory Deputy Leader since 2024. Subject to confirmation at the full Council meeting, he will take up the political leadership of the Council The Leader has ultimate responsibility for setting the long-term vision for the Council at the heart of Manchester’s ongoing inclusive growth, leading a team of Executive (Cabinet) members. He will represent the Council – and the city – at regional, national and international lev Cllr Bridges’ political priority has been ensuring that Manchester’s young people have the best start in life and have the opportunities, through work and skills, to share in the city’s success Prior to becoming Deputy Leader in 2024, Cllr Bridges had held the position of Executive Member for Children and Schools and overseen significant improvements across children’s services – which are now rated Outstanding by Ofsted. This included championing free school meals durin His commitment has been accentuated by his role as a parent to two toddlers, a daughter (aged three) and a son (aged four.)

Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. candidates.lead: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.evidence_text: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council Living alone for the first time can be a daunting experience, but it can be an even greater challenge for those who have grown up in care as some may only have a limited support network that they can rely on This can make adjusting to new responsibilities such as paying utility bills, managing a tenancy agreement, budgeting and keeping on top of household chores harder However, through the help of the local authority’s trainer flat scheme, of which there are now 14 across the borough, cared for young people aged 17 and over are being offered the perfect stepping stone to safely prepare for life on their own Fully furnished and equipped with everyday household goods, these flats provide young people with the time and support they need to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to successfully transition into adulthood This support is offered without the financial pressures normally associated with setting up a home, with the young people not required to contribute towards gas, electricity, water and other property-related utility costs until they turn 18

candidates.evidence_text: A 19th century manor house in Rochdale, which has lain empty for decades, has been transformed into a café, which will formally open this weekend Nestled in the heart of Denehurst Park, the café will occupy the ground floor of Denehurst House and visitors can see it for themselves when it formally opens its doors this Saturday (5 September) More than just a café, the new venue will be managed and run by local Community Interest Company, Get Together After Serving (GTAS), and will be staffed entirely by former armed forces personnel and their families Set up by Rochdale residents, Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor and Wayne Simms, GTAS aims to support the local veteran community in a number of ways, including through wellbeing programmes and local events and get-togethers Customers can expect café favourites like hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts and tea and coffee, alongside generous opening hours and honest prices. The team is also hoping to team up with other local businesses to do specials on Fridays, like curry, pizza and pies. With The building has been transformed by its owners, Rochdale Borough Council, who commissioned local builders, H Bell and Sons, alongside interior design specialists, to renovate the building while honouring its period features, which include ornate coving and bay windows

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . By a Thread was created to bring a new dimension to these ‘acrobatic’ relationships, and the parallels they draw to our everyda The relationships between ensemble members on stage mimic the everyday relationships we have as human beings. candidates.evidence_text: GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones Quiz on the Docks is landing at GRUB on Wednesday 23rd September , bringing together food, drinks, a bit of friendly competition and a £100 GRUB bar tab up for grabs

candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

candidates.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this November Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Tickets go on sale Fri 11 Sep. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Like few before him, he’s using that hunt to think about what it means to be an artist The Yěrén – an ape-like ‘wild man’ said to roam the mountains of Hubei province – is a centuries-old fixture of Chinese folklore that resurfaced after the Cultural Revolution, when sightings multiplied into what became known as ‘Yěrén fever’ and culminated in the largest organise Emerging at a moment when Chinese society was renegotiating the place of culture and creativity, this elusive ‘wild man’ has become, for Yuan, a stand-in for the artist: “a figure both visible and othered, alternately mythologised, pursued, and misunderstood” The exhibition’s new commission, Two Improvisations: A Punk Musical , runs across two channels. candidates.evidence_text: 8 ноября 2026 года в Indigo at The O2 состоится концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне Имя Горана Бреговича давно стало символом целого музыкального мира. Его путь начался в многонациональном Сараеве, где восточные мотивы естественно переплетались с западными традициями, а каждая улица имела свой ритм. Именно эта атмосфера сформировала композитора, впоследствии воз Впоследствии музыка Бреговича вышла за рамки концертных площадок. Сотрудничество с режиссером Emir Kusturica подарило мировому кинематографу саундтреки, ставшие неотъемлемой частью фильмов Time of the Gypsies, Arizona Dream и Underground. В этих мелодиях живут Балканы — с их своб Популярность Бреговича родилась не только благодаря знаменитым композициям “Kalashnikov”, “Ederlezi”, “In the Death Car” или “Bella Ciao”. Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! Город, который веками принимал выступления и разные культуры со всех континентов, на один вечер станет местом встречи британской сдержанности и безудержной балканской страсти. И, возможно, именно эта неожиданная Чтобы попасть на концерт GORAN BREGOVIC в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Еще больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. The 74-cover restaurant also features a private dining room for up to 12 guests, while t The restaurant focuses on exceptional produce sourced from trusted farmers, growers and suppliers, with classical techniques allowing the quality of the ingredients to take centre stage.
